rawRetro.summary: Implemented the device after-sales service and inspection coordination application (issue #497) directly in the application: migrations and idempotent seeds for customers, devices, work orders, events/operations, knowledge articles, manuals, inspections, attachments and engineer teams; a Workflow-driven auto-acceptance package (priority branch, SLA, in-app notification, idempotency); business permissions through composite resources, record-access scopes and sharing rules; server routes for tickets, knowledge, inspections, dashboard, attachments, directory, external device-platform API and the AI assistant; and the bilingual client pages. Verified with unit tests and a live runtime smoke pass over every requirement area. Two genuine runtime defects were found and fixed during smoke testing (create/update read-back required read permission; temporary sharing of an integer-primary-key record), and the remaining blocker is the absence of any configured LLM/embedding service.

blockers.title: AI knowledge-base Q&A cannot return generated answers or vectorize manuals
blockers.symptom: POST /service/assistant/ask always returns ai.status='blocked' with reason 'No language model service is connected'; the AI Knowledge Base manifests cannot be initiated/vectorized.
blockers.rootCause: The application has no llmServices configured (server/config/ai.ts llmServices: []) and no embedding model or vector database. The Knowledge Base manifests are configured in config.yml, which is out of scope to edit, and initiation additionally requires an LLM service and embedding model that do not exist in this environment.
blockers.resolution: Implemented the assistant endpoint and knowledge/manual keyword search over the application's own tables, and reported the AI generation capability honestly as blocked instead of fabricating answers. When an LLM and embedding service are configured, the interface is ready to consume them.

improvements: Framework gap discovered: a sharing rule's built-in `selection.records(ids)` compares the primary key as strings, so it fails validation for an integer primary key with `Filter value is invalid for Field "id" of type "integer"`. Worked around in application code by registering a parameterized record access (`service.sharedTicket`) whose resolver emits a numeric `$eq` condition. A framework-level fix would let record selections carry typed identifiers, or defer type coercion to the field.

Documented pitfall for future work: `pnpm nocobase db apply` runs migrations and seeds but does not boot application providers, so provider `boot()` registrations (workflow provisioning, scheduler targets, record accesses) only take effect when the real server starts.

`repository.createOne` and `repository.updateOne` both read the written row back through `readContext`, so any `create`/`update` permission must also grant `read`; a mutation-only permission fails at runtime with READ_FORBIDDEN.
Seed files loaded from source must import siblings with a `.ts` extension because `@nocobase/db` loads them with a direct Node `import()`, bypassing the TypeScript transform pipeline.
